correctness.summary: The finite-time absorption proof is correct under its explicit specialization. Differentiating the exact quadratic hypergradient gives h'(p)=a(p-x/(ax+B)); with learning rate 1/a the projected update is exactly p+=Pi_[0,1/a](x/(ax+B)). The null step makes |x| nonincreasing, so |ax|<b_min is invariant and the denominator never vanishes. For x>0, a negative atom resets p to zero without moving x, then two copies of the same positive atom first set p=x/(ax+b) and then hit zero exactly; the symmetric three-draw pattern works for x<0. Its conditional probability is at least q in every disjoint three-step block, yielding P(T>3m)<=(1-q)^m and E[T]<=3/q. The finite-sum probability lower bound and the fixed-step SGD mean-square noise floor also recompute as stated.

limitations: The result is one-dimensional, local, and uses the exact curvature scale in both the learning rate and candidate interval.
It requires exact full-objective comparisons and finite atomic noise; the repeated-atom proof does not extend to nonatomic noise.
The theorem is a special-case answer to the persistent-noise question, not a general OSGM convergence theorem.

originality.summary: The current OSGM-SGD paper explicitly leaves convergence under non-vanishing gradient noise as an open direction. Earlier stochastic mirror-descent work proves finite-time hitting under persistent noise at sharp minima, but a smooth quadratic is not sharp and the mechanism here is different: exact-function null steps plus atomic repeated-noise hypergradient feedback. Searches did not locate this particular OSGM absorption theorem. Originality is accepted only for the stated highly specialized mechanism.

scientific_value.summary: The theorem gives an exact positive example inside a regime the parent OSGM analysis does not cover and contrasts it cleanly with the stationary noise floor of fixed nonzero-step SGD. Its value is as a sharp boundary example, not as a general solution of persistent-noise stochastic optimization.
